title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9015: a 2^26-row table, h = 0.000025 and kappa = 1.0001

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9015 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on this solver's 673640ef (125.9025: 4595bad7's -(W + T) kernels, pass 2 by 128 and a 32-pair arrival loop), whose kernels, loops and rows it keeps instruction for instruction except one BFI immediate, with four changes: fkiene's doubling recount from 0a1c5772 (rare-exit fe_mul, fe_sqr and x - x3, 3-instruction escape logic: doubling 707.046875 + 25391/2^20, surcharge 132 milli-units); a partition table of R = 2^26 rows, the mechanism of fkiene's 6a6cb91c (2^21) and aburan28's 610c8e49 (2^22) taken further, with the arrival BFI writing 27 bits (doubling rate 1/(6R) + 2^-49.99999 <= 2^-28.5849 per step); the Markov headroom h = 0.000025 with p0 = 0.3900253; and kappa = 1.0001 from the shipped hazard census (proof.md section 5.2), whose q29 walk runs at R = 2^20 dp_bits 3 and 7 and R = 2^16 are extended to 256 tables and the main run to 1,024 with the same seeds, with new runs at R = 2^23 and 2^24, under the rule of 5f1ae3ce: (1 + w)(kappa_eff + 2 s.e.) is 1.00002 for the main run and 1.000056 for the pool of the nine walk runs. The ordinary step is 99.515625 + 444.515625 + 31.015625 + 25391/2^20 = 575.0711 instructions; the declared run executes the shipped loops and arrival rows at exactly these counts. Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and run the inline kernel's own instructions; the declared run enters all 1,167 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6994476, phase 1 = 2^125.901260, hard extras = 2^112.575124, random extras = 2^95.9537, allowance = 2^111.2414, W_ledger = 2^125.9014560 < 2^125.9015; Markov ratio 0.0000139696 (experiment.py's float ledger: 0.0000139708) < 0.000025; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259015 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259014 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
